questions.question: Define diffusion and use the particle model to explain why a crystal of potassium permanganate eventually colours a whole beaker of still water evenly. What happens to the particles once the colour is even?
questions.expected_answer: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration, caused by their random motion, until they are evenly spread. Water and permanganate particles are always moving randomly and colliding. Near the crystal there are many purple particles (high concentration) and elsewhere few (low), so more particles happen to move outward than inward, giving a net outward movement and spreading the colour. Once the colour is even, the particles keep moving randomly, but equal numbers cross any region in each direction, so there is no net movement.

questions.question: Describe the ammonia and hydrogen chloride experiment and explain the position of the white ring. Explain why gas particles moving at about 500 m/s still diffuse across a room slowly.
questions.expected_answer: Cotton wool soaked in ammonia solution is placed at one end of a long tube and cotton wool soaked in hydrochloric acid at the other, at the same time; the ends are sealed (in a fume cupboard). The gases diffuse along the tube and where they meet a white ring of ammonium chloride forms, well past the middle, nearer the hydrochloric acid end. Ammonia particles (relative mass 17) are lighter than hydrogen chloride particles (36.5), so they move faster and travel further in the same time. Although gas particles are fast, each collides with others billions of times per second, changing direction each time, so its path is a zigzag random walk with slow overall progress.

questions.question: List four factors that affect the rate of diffusion, explaining each with the particle model, and describe how diffusion allows gas exchange in the alveoli.
questions.expected_answer: Temperature: higher temperature, faster particles, faster diffusion. Particle mass: lighter particles move faster at the same temperature, diffusing faster. State: fastest in gases (far apart, fast), slower in liquids (close, constant collisions), slowest in solids (vibrate in place). Concentration difference: a larger difference gives a faster net movement. Distance: diffusion is fast over short distances and very slow over long ones. Alveoli: air in the alveoli has a higher oxygen concentration than the blood, so oxygen diffuses into the blood; blood has a higher carbon dioxide concentration, so carbon dioxide diffuses into the alveoli to be breathed out; walls one cell thick and a huge surface area make diffusion fast.
